title: A component that is out for repair on an issued purchase order can be transferred to another Flight Program, after which the order cannot receive it back and the component stays locked as out for repair
steps: 1. In program A add an uninstalled serialized component, raise a repair request for it, add it to a PO, issue the PO and record the outbound shipment (component shows Out for repair). 2. As system administrator transfer the component to program B (Flight Program transfer, kind component). 3. In program A open the PO and receive the unit back with its original serial.
expected: The transfer is refused while the component is out for repair or tied to an open repair PO line (as aircraft wait for open parts requests and locations for open PO lines), or the receipt still works.
actual: The transfer succeeds. The receipt is refused with 'Receive the original shipped component using its existing serial number.' because the PO mutation only loads program A's records. The component in program B keeps outForRepair pointing at program A's PO, so it cannot be edited ('Receive the component from repair before editing it.') or shipped again; the repair request in A stays 'Out for repair'. Program A can now cancel the PO (the out-for-repair guard no longer sees the component), leaving the component locked with no order. Only transferring the component back unblocks it. In the demo (all programs in one snapshot) the receipt instead succeeds and stores the program-B component in program A's location.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-transfer.test.ts (test PT-1 fails with the ConvexError above); src/domain/programTransfers.ts:140-156 (claimRecord checks only installed and linked inspections); convex/programs.ts:167-172 (loadCommitments loads no requests or orders for kind component); src/domain/purchaseOrders.ts:929-943 (shippedComponent).
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-transfer.test.ts convex/ && npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-pt-transfer.test.ts. Same gap before shipment: a component on an issued-but-unshipped repair PO, or with an open repair request, also transfers; the PO then fails validateRequestAllocations ('Repair PO lines must reference one existing component...') on every later command in the program? (not verified on server). Fix needs convex/programs.ts loadCommitments to load orders for components too.

title: An aircraft named on an issued purchase-order line can be transferred to another Flight Program, after which the order can be neither shipped nor received
steps: 1. In program A create a PO from an inspection ('Create PO for parts') or with a line linked to an aircraft, with no parts request. Issue it and record the shipment. 2. As system administrator transfer that aircraft to program B (allowed: it has no open parts requests). 3. Back in program A, receive the delivery on the PO.
expected: Either the transfer is refused while an issued PO line with outstanding quantity names the aircraft (the transfer already waits for open parts requests 'because reservations and orders point at this program'), or the delivery can still be received into program A's stock.
actual: Transfer succeeds. Receive and Record shipment are both refused with 'Aircraft is outside this Flight Program.' Once a shipment or partial receipt exists the order cannot return to draft either, so the only way out is to cancel the outstanding quantity and re-order; the parts that arrive cannot be booked against the PO.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-transfer.test.ts (test PT-2 fails with ConvexError 'Aircraft is outside this Flight Program.'); src/domain/purchaseOrders.ts:764 (moveOrder re-runs validateLines on every ship/receive) and :537-543; src/domain/programTransfers.ts:100-105 (only open parts requests block an aircraft).
notes: Same root cause as PT-3: moveOrder re-validates draft-time line links (stock identity, aircraft, inspection, work order) at ship/receive time, so any later change to those records strands an issued order.

title: Correcting a stock item's part number (or category) after its purchase order is issued makes the order impossible to ship or receive
steps: 1. Inventory: stock item FILTER at Store. 2. Create a PO line for that stock item, issue the PO, record the shipment. 3. Inventory > Details on the stock item: correct the part number to FILTER-48110 and save (accepted). 4. Open the PO and receive the delivery.
expected: The stock edit is refused while an issued order line with outstanding quantity points at the lot (as it is for reserved stock), or the receipt still books the delivery.
actual: Receipt (and any further shipment) is refused with 'Selected stock must match the part, category and location.' Because a shipment exists the order cannot return to draft, so the buyer must either rename the stock item back or cancel the outstanding quantity. Nothing on the stock form warns that the lot is on order.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts test PT-3; src/domain/purchaseOrders.ts:764 (moveOrder calls validateLines on an issued order) and :564-575 (matchesStock); src/domain/management/records.ts:161-181 (prepareStock guards reservations only).
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts (the server runs the same applier: convex/purchaseOrders.ts:47, convex/partsRequests.ts:50). Same root cause as PT-2.

title: Editing a component that sits on a draft or issued repair PO makes every purchase-order command in the Flight Program fail, with a message that does not name the order
steps: 1. Add an uninstalled serialized component ALT-1 S/N S1. 2. Raise a repair request for it and add it to a PO (save the draft; issuing is optional). 3. Components/Inventory: edit the component and correct its part number to ALT-1A (accepted: only a component already shipped is locked). 4. Try to save, issue, ship, receive or close ANY other purchase order in the program.
expected: The component edit is refused while a live repair PO line names it, or only the affected repair order is refused, with a message naming it.
actual: Every PO command in the program is refused with 'Repair PO lines must reference one existing component and its repair request.' because validateRequestAllocations re-checks every order in the program after each command. Receiving unrelated deliveries is blocked until someone works out which repair PO is stale and cancels it (cancel still works). The same lock follows any change that breaks checkRepairLine: a different part number, the component being installed or attached to an assembly, or transferred to another program before shipment (PT-1).
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts test PT-4; src/domain/purchaseOrders.ts:386 and :442-450 (validateRequestAllocations over all orders), :1239-1265 (checkRepairLine); src/domain/management/records.ts:120-143 (prepareComponent refuses only prior.outForRepair).
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts (the server runs the same applier: convex/purchaseOrders.ts:47, convex/partsRequests.ts:50).

title: After its purchase order is cancelled, a parts request can never change vendor, currency, ship-to or lines, and cannot be ordered from another vendor
steps: 1. Create a parts request with preferred vendor 'Vendor A'. 2. Add it to a PO, issue the PO. 3. Vendor A cannot supply: cancel the PO with a reason. The request returns to 'Requested' with the full quantity to order. 4. Edit the request and change the vendor to 'Vendor B' (or change a quantity). 5. Alternatively add the request to a new PO for Vendor B.
expected: With nothing reserved, issued or on order, the request can be re-sourced: docs/parts-and-repair-requests.md says lines and purchasing details are fixed 'once reserved, issued or allocated to a PO; release reservations and remove draft allocations before editing'.
actual: Step 4 is refused: 'Release reservations and remove draft PO allocations before changing lines or purchasing details...' although there is no reservation and no draft allocation to remove (isCommitted counts the allocation on the cancelled order for ever). Step 5 is refused: 'Request vendor, currency and ship-to must match the PO.' The request can only ever be re-ordered from Vendor A; otherwise it must be cancelled and re-entered, losing its link and number.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts test PT-5; src/domain/partsRequests.ts:831-839 (isCommitted counts allocations on cancelled and closed orders), :825-828; src/domain/purchaseOrders.ts:1288-1292.
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts (the server runs the same applier: convex/purchaseOrders.ts:47, convex/partsRequests.ts:50). Editing notes only is still accepted. The same freeze applies after a partial receipt whose remainder was cancelled.

title: A purchase-order receipt or shipment can be dated years before the order was created
steps: 1. Create and issue a PO today. 2. Receive parts and enter the receipt date 1999-01-01.
expected: Refused: a receipt cannot precede the order's issue (future dates are refused, and a repair return may not precede its shipment).
actual: Accepted; the receipt, the new stock lot's history and any core-return due date (receipt date + core days, so already years overdue) carry 1999-01-01.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts test PT-6; src/domain/purchaseOrders.ts:765-766 (only the future is checked).
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-orders.test.ts (the server runs the same applier: convex/purchaseOrders.ts:47, convex/partsRequests.ts:50). Back-dating to before today is legitimate (late entry); the question is whether dates before the issue date should be refused. A receipt may also be dated before its shipment.

title: The board view and the Costs screen put issued parts in different years or quarters, because part issues are dated in the runtime's time zone (server UTC for the board, the browser's zone for Costs)
steps: 1. Stock lot with unit cost $5,000. 2. At 19:00 US Central on 31 Dec 2026 (01:00 UTC on 1 Jan 2027) issue one unit to a parts request on a work-order task. 3. Administrator in Chicago opens Costs > that aircraft > 2026: the $5,000 is in 2026 spend and budget status. 4. In January a board member opens the board view.
expected: Both screens attribute the issue to the same year and quarter, so the board's 'this year' and 'this quarter' spend equal the Costs screen for the same period.
actual: The board view's totals come from the Convex server (boardSnapshot in convex/operations.ts via scopedSnapshot), where localDate(issue.at) is the UTC date 2027-01-01, so the same $5,000 is counted again in the board's 2027 year and Q1 spend and against the 2027 budget, while the Costs screen shows it in 2026. Every quarter end has the same 5 to 8 hour window for US zones. Two administrators in different time zones also see different period totals. Labor and other costs carry an entered date and are not affected.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-cost-period.test.ts (fails: board 2027 yearCents 500000, expected 0); src/domain/costs/workOrderCosts.ts:62 (date: localDate(i.at)); src/domain/model.ts:508 (localDate is device zone in the browser, UTC on the server); src/domain/boardView.ts:90-111; src/domain/programs.ts:283.
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-cost-period.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-cost-period.test.ts. Related, not proven: the server picks the board's current year and quarter from its own UTC clock inside a cached Convex query (boardSnapshot(s, today = localDate())), so on the evening of a quarter's last day US board members already see the next quarter, and the cached result may not roll over at midnight until some record changes.

title: 'Create PO for parts' on an inspection counts expired and reserved stock as on hand, so it suggests ordering nothing while the inspection's own parts check shows a shortage
steps: 1. Inventory: lot FILTER-1, quantity 2, expiration date in the past (or 2 reserved for another parts request). 2. Give an inspection a required part of 2 x that lot: the inspection shows it short by 2 (expired stock is never available). 3. On the inspection choose 'Create PO for parts'.
expected: Suggested quantity 2: the same shortage the parts check reports (docs/parts-and-repair-requests.md: stock past its expiration date 'counts toward the shortage').
actual: Suggested quantity 0 with 'On hand: 2 · On order: 0 · Required: 2'; saving as suggested is refused with 'Select at least one part quantity to purchase.' The buyer is told nothing needs ordering for stock that cannot be issued. Same class as inv-1 of the 3 Nov hunt, on the purchasing path.
evidence: repro/parts/pt8-create-po-expired.js (browser, REPRODUCED: inspection row says 'FILTER-1 · Main store · Need 2 / Available 0 · Short 2 · Expired 2', the dialog suggests quantity 0 with 'On hand: 2 · On order: 0 · Required: 2'); shots/parts-pt8-dialog.png; repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-shortfall.test.ts (domain, both tests fail); src/domain/purchaseOrderRules.ts:104-108; src/components/PurchaseOrders.tsx:2070-2083 and :1107-1109.
notes: Browser: cd repro/parts && node pt8-create-po-expired.js. Domain: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-shortfall.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-shortfall.test.ts. Severity lowered from Medium in round 2: the button only shows for an inspection that has a stored required-parts list, and no current form can create one (the inspection form carries it in a hidden field; Management.tsx:1336-1340). Such lists exist only in the hosted sample program (convex/sampleProgram.ts:470) or in records written through the API. docs/purchase-orders.md says suggestions 'deduct stock on hand', so the reserved-stock half may be intended; the expired half contradicts the shelf-life rule.

title: A stock-replenishment parts request can never be completed: received parts stay reserved for the request itself, releasing them shows 'On purchase order' with the full quantity to buy again, and the only way to 'Fulfilled' is to issue the new stock out of inventory
steps: 1. Inventory > a stock item > Parts / repair requests (or a plain stock request), priority P3 Stock, 2 x FILTER. 2. Add it to a PO, issue, receive 2, close the PO. The request shows 'Received / awaiting issue' and the 2 filters are Reserved 2 / Available 0, so no other request or work order can use them. 3. Release the reservation so the stock is usable.
expected: A request raised to restock a part is complete once its order is received; the received units are available stock and the request no longer asks to be ordered.
actual: After step 3 the request reads 'On purchase order' although its only PO is Closed and fully received, and its line shows 2 still to order (requestLineProgress.toOrder = 2), so it can be added to a second PO and bought twice. Leaving the reservation in place keeps the stock unavailable for ever. Issuing it makes the request 'Fulfilled' but removes the 2 units from on-hand stock, the opposite of restocking.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-stock-request.test.ts (fails: status 'On purchase order'); src/domain/partsRequests.ts:333-340 (toOrder adds back received units), :353-384 (requestStatus: 'Fulfilled' only when every line is issued; 'On purchase order' whenever anything was ever ordered); src/domain/purchaseOrders.ts:871-872 (every received allocation is reserved, stock requests included).
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-stock-request.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-stock-request.test.ts. The 'On purchase order' status after a release is wrong for aircraft requests too (received, then released: the closed PO still counts as 'ordered'); the stock-request case is the one with no correct way out. What 'fulfilled' should mean for a stock request needs the owner's call.

title: The purchase-order PDF silently replaces every character outside Latin-1 with a different character, so vendor names, delivery addresses and part descriptions sent to the vendor are wrong
steps: 1. Purchase orders > New PO. Vendor 'Łódź Aero' (Quick add). 2. Add a part 'AN3-5A', description 'Bolt ⅜ in ≥ 10 kΩ', quantity 4. Save the draft. 3. Open the PO: the screen shows the text correctly. 4. Save PO PDF (or Print PO) and read the PDF.
expected: The PDF prints the same text as the screen (docs/records-export.md and docs/logbook-entries.md use embedded DejaVu Sans 'so any character prints').
actual: The PDF prints 'Vendor: Aódz Aero' and '1. AN3-5A - Bolt !\ in "e 10 k©'. Each character outside Latin-1 is cut to its low byte (Ł->A, ź->z, Ż->{, ⅜->\, ≥->"e, Ω->©, №->!, CJK->random letters); no warning. A delivery address 'Żwirki i Wigury 1 №5, Łódź' prints as '{wirki i Wigury 1 !5 ... Aódz', and a long line then runs past the right margin. A size or rating in a part description changes meaning on the document the vendor fills the order from.
evidence: repro/parts/pt10-po-pdf-unicode.js (REPRODUCED); shots/parts-pt10-po.pdf, shots/parts-pt10-po-1.png, shots/parts-po-draft-top-1.png (address case); src/data/pdfLayout.ts:63 (doc.setFont('helvetica'), jsPDF's built-in WinAnsi font); src/data/poPdf.ts:52.
notes: Run: cd repro/parts && node pt10-po-pdf-unicode.js. paragraphPdf is shared, so the parts request / repair order / packing slip PDF (src/data/partsRequestPdf.ts:50) and the board summary PDF (documented as Helvetica) have the same substitution; not driven. Latin-1 accents (é, ö, Å, µ, Ø, ±, °) print correctly. Also seen: the PO PDF does not print an exchange line's core terms ('Exchange · core due N days' is on screen only).

title: Correcting a stock item's part number stops every job card that lists that lot as a part used from being saved, signed or completed
steps: 1. Job card on a work order: add a part used from inventory (stock item SEAL-1) and save. 2. Inventory administrator corrects the stock item's part number to SEAL-10. 3. The mechanic adds a remark, records a step result or signs off the job card and saves.
expected: The card saves: its parts list did not change. (A lot that expires after it was linked is deliberately kept so the card 'can still be edited, signed and completed'.)
actual: Every save of the card is refused with 'The part number must match the selected stock item.' until the mechanic re-selects the stock item on the card. Sign-offs and completion go through the same save, so they are blocked too. Sibling of PT-3: the stock form accepts the rename with no warning that orders and job cards point at the lot.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-jobcard-stock.test.ts (fails with that message); src/domain/taskCards.ts:804-805 (validatePartUsed runs for every part on every save) and :929-930; src/domain/management/records.ts:161-181.
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-jobcard-stock.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-jobcard-stock.test.ts. Other siblings checked in round 2: (a) an inspection or component requirement with a stored required-parts list cannot be edited after its stock location or its aircraft is transferred to another Flight Program ('Select a part and inventory location in this Flight Program.'), and no form can remove the list (hidden field); reachable only on sample-program or API-written data, so not filed separately. (b) A job card whose lot moved program is refused the same way; that refusal is pinned by src/domain/taskCards.test.ts:457 as intended.

title: Editing a stock item's unit cost re-prices every part ever issued from it, so closed work orders, past years' spend and budget status change after the fact
steps: 1. Lot CYL-1 with unit cost $1,000. In June 2025 issue 2 to a parts request on a work-order task; the work order is completed. Costs > aircraft > 2025 shows $2,000 parts. 2. In 2026 the vendor's price rises; the inventory administrator edits the lot's Cost to $1,500 (or corrects it for stock received later at a new price). 3. Open Costs for 2025, the work order's cost summary, the CSV export or the board view.
expected: The 2025 figures stay $2,000: the price of a part is fixed when it is issued, as a labor entry keeps the rate it was logged at (src/domain/costs/commands.ts:201).
actual: 2025 parts spend, the completed work order's total, cost per flight hour, budget status and the board's totals all become $3,000. There is no record of the cost at issue: the issue stores only stock, line and quantity. The reverse also happens: a PO receipt into an existing lot at a new price keeps the old lot cost (docs/purchase-orders.md), so later issues are priced at the old cost.
evidence: repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-cost-retro.test.ts (fails: 300000, expected 200000); src/domain/costs/workOrderCosts.ts:160-171 (priceIssue reads the lot's current cost); src/domain/partsRequests.ts:1047-1053 (an issue records no unit cost).
notes: Run: cp repro/parts/zz-hunt-pt-cost-retro.test.ts src/domain/ && npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-pt-cost-retro.test.ts. A manual part unit cost on the work order wins over the stock cost, but it can only be set while the work order is open (openOrder in costs/commands.ts). Labor is not affected: each entry keeps its own rate, and a labor-rate change applies to new entries only (checked by reading; entries logged before any rate is set stay at $0).
